title: Build the story. Test the numbers.
subtitle: A guided valuation inspired by Aswath Damodaran’s published approach. Independent educational tool; no affiliation or endorsement.

steps.title: Company, date & evidence
steps.question: What are we valuing?
steps.why: Start with the business, its reporting date, currency and the share you own. A filing describes a past period; a valuation belongs to your chosen date.
steps.challenge: Which facts are current enough for this decision?

steps.title: Business & starting point
steps.question: How does this business make money, and what earnings are repeatable?
steps.why: Numbers need an economic story. Adjustments should reflect the business, not make it appear more profitable.
topics: Today / what changes / what could break
steps.challenge: Does this one-off cost keep returning?

steps.title: Revenue & growth
steps.question: How big can the business realistically become?
steps.why: Growth comes from customers, capacity, prices or products. Your final revenue should fit a plausible market.
steps.challenge: What market share or capacity does your forecast imply?

steps.title: Margins & taxes
steps.question: What can the business keep from each dollar of sales?
steps.why: Competition and costs determine how much growth becomes operating profit. Cash-tax relief needs evidence and timing.
steps.challenge: What lets margins improve, and what limits them?

steps.title: Reinvestment & funding
steps.question: What must the company reinvest to deliver that growth?
steps.why: Factories, data centers, R&D and working capital use cash. Faster growth is not free.
topics: Capital lead time and funding needs
steps.challenge: For each extra dollar of sales, how much new capital is needed?

steps.title: Risk & mature economics
steps.question: What return is required, and what survives after fast growth ends?
steps.why: Risk must match the cash-flow currency. Stable growth still needs investment and a credible mature business.
steps.challenge: Why would excess returns persist, and how will competition change them?

steps.title: Equity & share claim
steps.question: How much of the operating value belongs to this share?
steps.why: Cash, debt and other claims must be counted once. The share count must match the security you are valuing.
topics: Share count, awards, splits and ADR ratio
steps.challenge: Does every asset and obligation appear exactly once?

steps.title: Challenge & review
steps.question: What would have to be true for your estimate to be wrong?
steps.why: Coherent scenarios reveal uncertainty. Saving the original lets you learn whether the story, evidence or expectations changed.
steps.challenge: What new evidence would make you revise your story?

labels.researchOnly: Recorded for review; not yet included in the calculation.
labels.simplifiedInvestment: Simplified reinvestment: growth-linked sales/capital does not separately model asset replacement or capital lead times.

readinessPolicy.principle: A nuance is not automatically a hard block. Distinguish immaterial/not-applicable, manually supported simplification, and unsupported material mechanics. Allow research and drafts regardless; withhold a complete-model claim where material economics are missing.
blocking: Unavailable or future-dated source used as eligible fact
Unresolved currency/security/ADR claim conversion for per-share value
Material unmodeled mechanics without explicit limitation/manual evidence
review: Replacement capex and capital lead-time materiality

companyPrompts.NBIS: Review business perimeter, capacity/power investment, utilization ramp, replacement cycles, losses and tax use, financing and dilution. Record research; do not imply the simple engine models all of these.
companyPrompts.MU: Normalize memory price/volume/mix and full-cycle margins; support replacement investment and obsolescence assumptions.
companyPrompts.TSM: Verify reporting/valuation currency, dated FX and depositary-share ratio; reconcile fabrication capacity and investment.
companyPrompts.NVDA: Fabless still requires R&D and working capital; review supply commitments, SBC/awards, feasible market scale and marginal return fade.
companyPrompts.AAPL: Verify product and service economics, installed base, replacement cycle, channel inventory, manufacturing exposure, and cash/claims.
companyPrompts.MSFT: Verify subscription and cloud segment drivers, AI/data-center reinvestment and asset lives, central costs and stock compensation.
companyPrompts.AMZN: Separate retail and cloud economics; reconcile leases, fulfillment investment, working capital and segment overhead.
companyPrompts.GOOG: Examine search/advertising economics, cloud and other bets, AI effects on costs/capex, and common-class economic rights.
companyPrompts.META: Examine advertising monetization and engagement, infrastructure reinvestment, long-horizon losses and stock compensation.
companyPrompts.TSLA: Separate automotive price/volume/capacity and energy. Optional businesses need explicit probability, costs and no double counting.
companyPrompts.COHR: Review optical/customer mix, manufacturing capacity/yields and the derived operating-income subtotal. Investigate gains, restructuring and impairments without assuming they are nonrecurring.
companyPrompts.LITE: Review optical product/customer mix, concentration, manufacturing capacity and capex lead time; reconcile acquisition and restructuring effects.
companyPrompts.AAOI: Review optical product/customer mix, customer concentration, manufacturing yields, capacity and funding needs.
companyPrompts.AVGO: Separate semiconductor and software economics; review acquisition amortization, debt/claims, R&D, concentration and shared costs.
